name: Magic Link (Passwordless)
description: HMAC-SHA256 signed single-use tokens, Resend/Nodemailer transport, 10k-entry LRU replay store, AES-256-GCM stateless session cookie, and a root middleware that protects configured paths while still honouring AUTH_MODE=mock as a dev short-circuit.

questions.prompt: From address for magic link emails?
Application base URL (used to build the magic link)?
Path prefixes the middleware should require auth for (comma-separated)?

checklist: If using Resend: sign up at https://resend.com and set RESEND_API_KEY
If using Nodemailer: run npm install nodemailer and configure SMTP_* env vars
Set MAGIC_LINK_FROM to a verified sender address for your transport
Set AUTH_MODE=real (or unset AUTH_MODE) — this template's middleware.ts overwrites auth-mock's dev middleware and runs real magic-link auth on protected paths
Keep AUTH_MODE=mock for local dev — both the middleware and getCurrentUser() short-circuit to MOCK_USER
Test flow: POST /api/auth/magic-link/request { email } → check inbox → GET /api/auth/magic-link/verify?token=... → /dashboard
Verify second use of same link returns 'already used' redirect
Verify GET /api/auth/me returns UserContext after login
Verify DELETE /api/auth/logout clears the session cookie
Confirm middleware redirects unauthenticated requests to /login for paths under {protected_paths}
Use getCurrentUser() / requireAuth() in Server Components and Server Actions
